summary.headline: Go Digit's Q1 FY27 GDPI fell 8% and loss ratio rose to 73.3%, with management choosing profitability over growth.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a deliberately soft quarter, with gross written premium down 8% (about -2% excluding inward reinsurance in group health and crop). Motor own damage, mainly private car, drove the loss ratio up from 70.3% to 73.3%, and management said it had made the wrong call on the stand-alone OD renewals. On its internal KPI basis (NEP with DAC, excluding MTM and discounting), PAT was INR190 crore versus INR200 crore a year ago and combined ratio was 107.2%. Under Indian Accounting Standards (IFRS-style prescribed format), PAT rose to INR372 crore from INR325 crore, helped by unrealised gains and discounting.

segments.name: Motor own damage (private car)
segments.commentary: Primary driver of the loss ratio increase; management cut stand-alone OD and non-new car business, with stabilisation expected in Q2 FY27. Motor overall grew 0.4%, with 2-wheeler growing strongly and private car and CV together down about 27%.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: CV share of motor fell to about 23-24% from roughly 65% four to five years ago, as the company deliberately exited the segment.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: GDPI down 37% against an industry decline of about 27-28%. Gross fire loss ratio was 67% in Q1 despite one large claim; retention is about 20%.

segments.name: Third-party motor
segments.commentary: TP loss ratio 66.6%, broadly stable. Market share was cut from April, with a view that a TP rate hike of 90-95% of vehicles is needed.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Loss ratio rose year on year, attributed to one large bank-driven personal accident policy. Group health and crop inward reinsurance were not renewed on pricing grounds.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it does not guide and will not assume that market conditions normalise in the current or next quarter.
Management is assuming soft market conditions persist at least until 31 March 2027.
Own damage loss ratio expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.
Management said that, excluding the drop in fire, the fourth quarter could see a base effect on growth.
Dividend: management said IGAAP solvency (about 242%) supports a dividend, to be considered by the Board in the last quarter, subject to RBC norms.
Underwriting and claims-settlement actions on TP were planned for around the third week of August 2026.
capex_capacity: Investment mix: 9.5% of AUM in equity, REITs and InvITs (AT1 bonds shown separately); management said it could take equity to 13-14% if markets fall, or to 15-18% in its stated framework.
Fixed income duration moved from 4.5 to 4.9 in Q1; reinvestment yield rose to 7.8% from 7.5%. Management said it would extend duration to about 5.2 if the 30-year yield moves above about 7.75%.
Reinsurance commission increased across all lines and reinsurance capacity increased, per management.
Management said it is waiting for RBC norms, expected possibly within FY27, to know whether solvency will be measured on RBC, IFRS or IGAAP.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing across most lines has fallen and is now down across the board. It cited EOM rules, which pushed commissions up, and low-priced crop, group health, and fire business written to meet EOM.
Claims inflation: no third-party motor rate increase for about five years, while minimum wages, parts, paint and labour costs have risen.
Fire rates were said to be down about 40-45%.
Management said Digit has not chased growth; it gave up fire and commercial business it judged underpriced, and said the 2W and bancassurance/digital channels were growing well.

Supreme Court (June 11, 2026) TP ruling: management said it is comfortable with reserves and will not take a bet on judgment interpretation; two High Court rulings (July 2 Allahabad, July 16 Karnataka) were cited as narrowing the ruling.
